knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

```{r model-meta, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(nlmixr2lib::readModelDb("Chiu_2014_tce_mouse_pbpk"))
cat("* Citation: ", ui$reference, "\n", sep = "")
cat("* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1289/ehp.1307623>\n")
```

* Description: `r ui$description`

Chiu and colleagues extended an existing whole-body physiologically based
pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model of trichloroethylene (TCE) and its metabolites to a
panel of genetically diverse mouse strains, in order to quantify the toxicokinetic
population variability that matters for human risk assessment. The structural
model is a modification of the Hack et al. (2006) / Evans et al. (2009) TCE PBPK
model: it adds one-compartment submodels for the glutathione-conjugation
metabolites S-(1,2-dichlorovinyl)glutathione (DCVG) and
S-(1,2-dichlorovinyl)-L-cysteine (DCVC), a two-compartment submodel for
dichloroacetic acid (DCA), and a revised DCA production route. The authors fit
the model with a hierarchical Bayesian population approach (eight MCMC chains to
160,000 iterations) estimating both parameter uncertainty and interstrain
variability.

This vignette implements the model for the single route the mouse data use --
an oral gavage of 2,100 mg/kg TCE in corn oil -- and for the B6C3F1/J *index*
strain against which all interstrain scaling is referenced. It is a deterministic
typical-value replication: the parameters are the posterior medians of the
population means (Supplemental Table S6), and every interstrain scaling parameter
`lnIS*` is held at 0 (its B6C3F1/J reference value).

## Structure

TCE is absorbed from a stomach and duodenum compartment into seven flow-limited
tissues (rapidly perfused, slowly perfused, fat, gut, liver, kidney, blood).
Arterial blood is the steady-state lung equation

$$C_{Art} = \frac{Q_C\,C_{Ven}}{Q_C + Q_P/P_B},$$

so volatile first-pass pulmonary elimination is captured without carrying a
respiratory-tract compartment (the inhalation, closed-chamber and intravenous
machinery of the full MCSim model is inactive for oral gavage and is omitted).
Hepatic TCE is split by saturable CYP oxidation into trichloroacetic acid (TCA),
trichloroethanol (TCOH) and a direct-DCA branch, and by a saturable
glutathione-conjugation branch into DCVG; renal glutathione conjugation adds a
parallel kidney source. TCOH feeds a two-tissue submodel with onward oxidation to
TCA and glucuronidation to trichloroethanol-glucuronide (TCOG, with biliary
recirculation); TCA is a protein-binding three-tissue submodel; DCA is a
two-compartment submodel; DCVG converts to DCVC.

Every ODE state is a paper-mechanistic amount (mg, except the DCVG amount in
mmol), so there is no canonical `central` compartment; the dose is an oral gavage
into `AStom`.

## Source trace

Model structure and ODEs are transcribed from the authors' published MCSim code
(Supplemental Material -- PBPK Model Code). Parameter provenance:

| Model element | Source |
| --- | --- |
| Physiologic baselines (flows, volumes, blood:plasma fraction) | Supplemental Table S3 / MCSim `Species == 3` (mouse) branch |
| TCE partition coefficients (blood:air, tissue:blood) | Supplemental Table S3 / MCSim `Species == 3` branch (scaling fixed) |
| Cardiac output, ventilation-perfusion (`lnQCC`, `lnVPRC`) | Supplemental Table S6 posterior medians |
| Hepatic oxidation `VMax`, `KM` (`lnVMaxC`, `lnKMC`) | Supplemental Table S6; derived B6C3F1/J medians main-text Table 2 |
| Oxidation splits (`lnFracOtherC`, `lnFracTCAC`) | Supplemental Table S6 posterior medians |
| Hepatic GSH conjugation (`lnVMaxDCVGC`, `lnClDCVGC`) | Supplemental Table S6; derived medians Table 2 |
| TCOH / TCA / TCOG / DCA / DCVG / DCVC rate constants | Supplemental Table S6 posterior medians |
| Effective distribution volumes (`lnPeffDCVG/DCVC/DCA`) | Supplemental Table S6 posterior medians (Table S3 note x) |
| Renal GSH conjugation, free-TCA tissue partitions | Supplemental Table S3 / MCSim defaults (fixed, not estimated) |
| Oral gavage 2,100 mg/kg; B6C3F1/J Table 2 total dose 76.4 mg | Materials and Methods; main-text Table 2 |

Every `ini()` entry carries an in-file comment pointing to the specific table,
posterior-median value and baseline it derives from.

# Virtual subject

The B6C3F1/J index strain, dosed by oral gavage at 2,100 mg/kg. The default body
weight of 0.0364 kg reproduces the 76.4 mg total dose reported in Table 2
(`76.4 / 2100 = 0.0364`).

```{r cohort}
mod <- nlmixr2lib::readModelDb("Chiu_2014_tce_mouse_pbpk")

BW <- 0.0364 # kg; reproduces the Table 2 total dose of 76.4 mg at 2100 mg/kg
dose_mg <- 2100 * BW

ev <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_mg, cmt = "AStom")
ev <- rxode2::et(ev, seq(0, 24, by = 0.1))
ev$WT <- BW
```

# Simulation

Deterministic typical-value solve (`zeroRe()`; the model carries no random
effects).

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev, returnType = "data.frame")
```

# Replicate Figure 4 -- B6C3F1/J serum metabolites

Figure 4 of Chiu et al. (2014) plots the four measured metabolites "in blood
(mmol/L)" for the B6C3F1/J strain (data from Kim et al. 2009b). The data points
below were digitised by the maintainers from that figure (approximate).

```{r fig4-data}
fig4 <- dplyr::tribble(
  ~metab, ~time, ~conc,
  "TCA", 0.5, 0.14, "TCA", 6, 0.37, "TCA", 8, 0.36, "TCA", 12, 0.33,
  "DCA", 0.5, 0.90e-4, "DCA", 2, 1.05e-4, "DCA", 6, 0.90e-4, "DCA", 8, 0.95e-4, "DCA", 12, 0.75e-4,
  "DCVG", 0.5, 3.3e-5, "DCVG", 2, 3.8e-5, "DCVG", 8, 0.3e-5, "DCVG", 24, 0.05e-5,
  "DCVC", 0.5, 0.3e-6, "DCVC", 2, 2.4e-6, "DCVC", 6, 0.85e-6, "DCVC", 8, 2.0e-6,
  "DCVC", 12, 0.5e-6, "DCVC", 24, 0.2e-6
)

pred <- sim |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    time,
    TCA = Cc_tca, DCA = Cc_dca, DCVG = Cc_dcvg, DCVC = Cc_dcvc
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "metab", values_to = "conc")

lvl <- c("TCA", "DCA", "DCVG", "DCVC")
pred$metab <- factor(pred$metab, levels = lvl)
fig4$metab <- factor(fig4$metab, levels = lvl)
```

```{r fig4-plot, fig.height = 5.5}
ggplot2::ggplot(pred, ggplot2::aes(time, conc)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.8) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = fig4, colour = "black", size = 1.8) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~metab, scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Concentration in blood (mmol/L)",
    title = "B6C3F1/J typical-value prediction (line) vs digitised Figure 4 data (points)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw()
```

The oxidative metabolites TCA and DCA track the published data closely. The
glutathione-conjugation metabolites DCVG and DCVC are reproduced in shape (an
early DCVG rise that clears by ~8 h; a DCVC peak at 2-3 h) but the typical-value
curve runs roughly 2-fold (DCVG) to 5-fold (DCVC) above the digitised points.
This is expected rather than an error: those parameters are very poorly
identified (the Table 2 posterior for the GSH `Km` spans 0.003 to 9.8 x 10^4
mg/L), so the median of each strongly-correlated *derived* quantity does not
equal the quantity evaluated at the median *scaling* parameters. The cumulative
metabolism check below -- the paper's headline quantitative output -- confirms
the parameterisation is correct.

# Validation against Table 2 -- cumulative metabolism

PKNCA is not meaningful here: the metabolites are formed, not dosed, so there is
no administered-dose AUC to normalise. The mechanistic validation instead compares
the model's cumulative metabolism dose-metrics (the published code's `AMetOX`,
`AMetGSH`, `TotTCAProd`, `TotDCAProd` outputs) against the B6C3F1/J posterior
medians and 95% credible intervals in main-text Table 2.

```{r table2}
ev2 <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_mg, cmt = "AStom")
ev2 <- rxode2::et(ev2, seq(0, 72, by = 0.5)) # integrate to near-complete metabolism
ev2$WT <- BW
end <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev2, returnType = "data.frame")
end <- end[nrow(end), ]

tca_mol <- end$AMetTCAprod / 163.5
dca_mol <- end$AMetDCAprod / 129.0

tab <- dplyr::tribble(
  ~`Metabolism metric`, ~Model, ~`Reported median (95% CI)`,
  "TCE oxidized (mg)", round(end$AMetOx, 1), "16 (5.5, 60)",
  "TCE conjugated with GSH (mg)", round(end$AMetGSH, 3), "0.05 (0.03, 0.5)",
  "TCA produced (mg)", round(end$AMetTCAprod, 2), "3.4 (1.4, 15)",
  "DCA produced (mg)", round(end$AMetDCAprod, 3), "0.3 (0.02, 3.7)",
  "Oxidation/GSH ratio (mg/mg)", round(end$AMetOx / end$AMetGSH), "290 (41, 1070)",
  "TCA/DCA ratio (mol/mol)", round(tca_mol / dca_mol, 1), "10 (0.9, 130)"
)
knitr::kable(tab)
```

All six metrics fall within the reported 95% credible intervals. The point
estimates sit above the posterior medians (again the median-composition effect),
but well inside the intervals, confirming that the extracted structure and
parameters reproduce the paper's quantitative findings: oxidation dominates
glutathione conjugation by roughly 300-fold, and TCA production exceeds DCA by
about an order of magnitude.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Index strain, typical value.** This file implements the B6C3F1/J *index*
  strain (interstrain scaling `lnIS* = 0`) at the posterior medians of the
  population means (Supplemental Table S6). The paper's hierarchical Bayesian
  model also estimated parameter uncertainty and interstrain variability (Tables
  S4-S6, with posterior CVs per parameter); those uncertainty and random-effects
  layers are documented but not carried as a simulation layer here, so there is
  no IIV and no residual error. The measurement-error variances were not reported
  as usable point estimates.
* **Oral gavage only.** The full MCSim model supports inhalation (open and closed
  chamber), intravenous, intra-arterial, portal-vein and drinking-water routes,
  plus direct TCA and TCOH dosing. Only the oral-gavage route used by the mouse
  data is implemented. The respiratory-tract and lung-oxidation compartments are
  omitted because they are inactive without inhalation; volatile pulmonary
  elimination is still captured through the steady-state arterial-blood equation.
* **Fixed (non-estimated) parameters.** Renal glutathione-conjugation parameters
  (`VMaxKidDCVG`, `KMKidDCVG`, `FracKidDCVC`) were fixed in the paper (they do not
  appear in Tables S4/S6) and are kept at their coded mouse defaults. The TCE
  partition coefficients and the free-TCA and TCOH/TCOG tissue partitions have
  their scaling parameters fixed (Table S3 notes k-r, t, v, w), so they equal the
  coded mouse baselines.
* **DCVG / DCVC magnitude.** As discussed above, the typical-value curves for
  DCVG and DCVC run 2- to 5-fold above the digitised Figure 4 points because
  those parameters are poorly identified (credible intervals spanning 3-5 orders
  of magnitude). Parameters were *not* tuned to the figure; the cumulative-metabolism
  check against Table 2 is the quantitative validation of record.
* **Body weight.** The default 0.0364 kg is back-calculated from the Table 2
  total dose (76.4 mg at 2,100 mg/kg); individual animal weights were not
  tabulated. Set `WT` and the gavage `amt` (`2100 * WT`) together to re-scale.
* **Blood vs serum.** The data are serum (= plasma) concentrations; Figure 4
  plots them "in blood", so the TCA output is the plasma concentration times the
  blood:plasma ratio `TCAPlas`, and all four outputs are in mmol/L to match the
  figure axes.
```
